steps.text: Firearms Workshop, Via Borgos, Pagus Faber

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Hello...? Anybody home?
Sculptures of saints line the walls of the small workshop, acting as makeshift display shelves, exhibiting guns to would-be customers in impossible arrangements.
But Amos does not see a single customer. No one stops at the door to the workshop, except for himself. His first feeling is that the whole place seems cold and cheerless.
Not even the proprietor is present. Gazing on the dim light cast upon the sculptures, his second feeling is one of eeriness.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Senior Paganini? Are you in?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: (Why would a gunsmith have such an absurd name?)
Amos looks around, then bumps into something.
He looks around and finds himself staring into a pair of massive, luminous eyes that peer straight at him from the shadows.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Eek—

steps.name: Massive Eyes
steps.text: Who are you, barging into my place like this—let me put my glasses on!

steps.name: Massive Eyes
steps.text: A functionary?

steps.name: Massive Eyes
steps.text: Sorry. I was taking a nap because there's been no business lately. I wasn't expecting an official visit.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I am Cardinal Aide Amos. I came to see that the handover of this Firearms Workshop is in order. And you are...?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: I'm Paganini. The guy with the absurd name.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Wait. You're a Liberi?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Do I look like a Sankta to you?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Sorry. What I meant is, I've never seen a Liberi in this line of work. After all, only Sankta use patron firearms—

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Got a problem with it?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Chefs don't necessarily eat their own cooking. I can't use the weapons I make, that's all.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Do you need my gunsmith's license? I must have made close to a thousand patron firearms for the people of Laterano, if not more. Maybe even yours...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Whew, this is some real 'premium' work. Well above my craftsmanship, that's for sure.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Not that it matters anymore. I'm about to close up shop.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: All recent orders have been cancelled. The Notarial Hall can have this last batch of guns.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Y-You've already prepared. I thought...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Thought I would be trouble? Thought I would give you a hard time?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Th-That's not what I meant.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: The registrar indicates that this workshop has been around for a century. As a Liberi who has chosen to make patron firearms for the Sankta, it must hold incredible significance to you—

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Save it. Anyone could tell that gunsmiths have become a dying breed these last few years. We've all been waiting for the day to come.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: If you're asking whether I like it or not: No, of course I don't like it. Do you want to hear about the insomnia I've had lately?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I can arrange a confessional for you, if you wish. The Seventh Tribunal will cover the cost.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: If anyone here needs a confession, it's you.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: This old man's set to retire. But my apprentice, Vannini, she hasn't even had the chance to make her own patron firearm.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: If all the Firearms Workshops are gone, you'll be responsible for her future.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Of course. Closing the Firearms Workshops is part of a process to make the firearms manufacturing more standardized and efficient. Gunsmiths like you and your apprentice remain valuable talent.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I will pass this on to the Sixth Tribunal, which is responsible for civil matters. Your apprentice, Vannini, should receive a recommendation to the Shrine of Gunsmithing in Pagus Michaelion, which is almost complete.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Shrine of Gunsmithing, huh...? I hope they're that confident when they actually start smithing guns.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I have faith in Laterano's...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Yeah, yeah, I've heard it too many times.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: ...If you have no objection, I would like to ask you to sign these papers.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Effective immediately, this workshop will cease operation, with the Notarial Hall handling follow-up matters.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Pleasant day to you, senior.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: See yourself out.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Pagus Faber, Via Borgos... how familiar.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: This is the place!

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: Has the connection been established?

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: I-I think so.

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: We've been waiting for two days on the outskirts. I want to go out and get some fresh air!

steps.name: Feline
steps.text: These Laterans invited us onto this mobile abbey while we were wandering in the wilderness, then made us wait like this once we got to Laterano.

steps.name: Busy Nun
steps.text: I apologize for keeping you waiting.

steps.name: Busy Nun
steps.text: Twelve other nomadic abbeys have reached Laterano, in addition to the busy schedule of the Summit of Nations. We beg your understanding.

steps.name: Busy Nun
steps.text: The Notarial Hall has prepared temporary accommodations in Pagus Ambrosius. Once you've settled down, the Sixth Tribunal will help you with your registration and social welfare.

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: S-Sister? Do you mean that outsiders like us will get to stay in Laterano?

steps.name: Busy Nun
steps.text: From the second Summit of Nations, Laterano's doors will be open to all races...

steps.name: Busy Nun
steps.text: You shall find a home in the city.
Hey, Extra! Are you alright?
I'll find a doctor!
No!
You can't let the Sankta find out, not yet...

steps.name: Busy Nun
steps.text: Please let me through.

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: D-Don't worry about it, Sister.

steps.name: Feline
steps.text: We can take care of this. You're busy, aren't you?

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: Argh—

steps.name: Busy Nun
steps.text: Are you... pregnant, Sarkaz?

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: Your people didn't stop the Sarkaz from entering the abbey! You're gonna make it a problem now?

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: You want me to go, I'll go! I don't need help from the Sankta!

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: You won't lay a hand on me or my baby!
You misunderstand. It's just we have no directive for accommodating pregnant mothers in the abbey's standard operating procedures, and thus Sister Angie is not sure what to do.
Allow me to bring her to the Shrine of Nurtury, Sister Angie.

steps.name: Busy Nun
steps.text: The Shrine of Nurtury is not yet open to the public. This is against regulations.

steps.name: Busy Nun
steps.text: Besides, what are you doing here?
Our Lord has guided me to where I should be.
We must have some flexibility. The Shrine of Nurtury cannot ignore an ailing mother.

steps.name: Busy Nun
steps.text: Yes, Matriarch.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I am Keph, Matriarch of the Shrine of Nurtury. Simply put, I am its caretaker.
The woman with golden hair turns slowly toward the Sarkaz. Her voice is soft yet crystal clear, seemingly carefully probing.
The Sarkaz sees the two black horns on the woman's head, then turns her gaze to the woman's eyes. She sees an empty void underneath the intricate patterns of the eyepatch.

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: What are you... Sarkaz? Sankta? Blind, too?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Sarkaz, Sankta... we have no need of these words of distinction. You and I, we are alike... like you, I am nurturing lives that I treasure.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: My lack of sight does not prevent me from perceiving you and the new life you carry... the anxiety and joy that it brings you.

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: We Sarkaz don't talk this way. You're Sankta, a strange Sankta with children.

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: Do you raise your children in that... Shrine of something? What kind of place is it?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: The Shrine of Nurtury, where new life is born and nurtured. You and I stand in its shadow.

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: A shrine... for giving birth?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Birth is sacred. Each new birth is a continuation of the Lateran faith. Only in this way may we shape the future.

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: I don't understand.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Long have you wandered the wilderness. You have not enjoyed the care that a mother should. You are weak... and so is your child.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Are you sure you want to leave the Holy City that is so near and return to the wilderness at a time like this?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Your name is 'Extra', madam?

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: You don't like it?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: We understand the difficulties facing the Sarkaz... many Sarkaz mothers name their children 'Extra', seeing them as nothing more than a little extra in their lives.

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: This name's got nothing to do with my mom. I took it myself after I got pregnant. Who's to say who's the extra?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: You got a problem?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: You treasure your bonds with your child. You are proud of having this little extra in your life, and you want everyone to know.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: This is a wonderful, noble sentiment, madam. It should not be tainted by racism or hatred.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I know what you fear.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: All people here in this abbey, Sankta, Feline, Kuranta, Lupo, and Vulpo alike bear witness.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: The Summit of Nations is underway. Countless outlanders from all nations have flocked to Laterano. Laterano would not be foolish enough to harm a pregnant mother with all this attention.

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: (Casts a glance)

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: You have my word.

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Thank you for your understanding.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Let us welcome the birth of a new life together in Laterano. It will bridge a gulf and bring new meaning. This birth will be a great achievement.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: This is why I have come... Our Lord has guided me to where I should be.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Welcome to Laterano... you are needed here, all of you.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Whatever it is you're after, I'm sure I can't help you.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I haven't said anything yet!

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Alright, Seniora Sankta, what do you want? Do you need your guardian gun fixed, or you want some custom ammo?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Go out the door and turn left. You might just find one of the last Firearms Workshops in Pagus Michaelion that hasn't shut down yet, if you can get there before the functionaries.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: I signed the handover documents from the Seventh Tribunal ten minutes ago. I'd be violating the Law if I did anything with this stuff now.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: What if I said I wanted to make an explosion that would shake the city?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Not interested.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Come on! You're Master Pag, the King of Gunsmiths! If anyone would want to see an explosion, it's you!

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Don't butter me up with a title you just made up on the spot.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I know what you're afraid of, Master Pag.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: All I need is a little help—lend me some equipment, some of your expert knowledge—to help me figure out what's going on in Laterano.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I'm really anxious about all this.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: My boss always says nothing gets in the way of Penguin Logistics completing our mission, or the after party!

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: You don't need to DO anything. That way, you won't be violating the Law, right?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Get your guardian gun away from my collection, Sankta.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Besides, I know this gun. I made the damned thing—

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Haha. Recognize it, don't you?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Then you also know how powerful it is.
I got Dr. Paola to make a new pair of glasses for you, magister! She admonished me to no end, she says it's your punishment to keep wearing those antiques of yours...
Here, try them on! Uh—
Wh-Who's this? What's going on, Magister Paganini?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Hey, if it isn't the quiet little girl! Look how fluently you can gab now!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: What was your name again? Vanheim? Vannessa? Oh, I know—

steps.name: Exusiai & Vannini
steps.text: —Vannini!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: See? We still got our teamwork!

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: I remember now! You're El! You came to pick your first patron firearm...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Magister Paganini never lets me bother the customers when they come to the shop. But there was such a ruckus outside that day, I couldn't help but peek...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Magister Paganini found me out, though. I don't remember much else because I was so scared he was going to yell at me... sorry!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Oh, so that's why? You were afraid...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Weird, I thought you looked happy.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: What brings you here today, El?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: (Winks)

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Vani.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: The Seventh Tribunal came today. My workshop is...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: I'm not officially a gunsmith yet. I don't actually work for this shop. It's not against the Law, strictly speaking.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Can I help this customer, Magister?

steps.name: Obstinate Child
steps.text: Gotcha, Senior Nurturer!

steps.name: Proud Child
steps.text: Where did you go? Romya said you were hiding from us. Is that true?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Of course not.

steps.name: Obstinate Child
steps.text: Then let's play Halo!
Father Andoain is very busy. How about you guys play with me?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Your Eminence.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I have some private matters to attend to. I'll be back soon.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: No need to be nervous. I have your leave request on file. What I really should ask is, what are you doing here with the children when you're supposed to be on leave?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I thought I had enough time for one round of Halo.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: And then? Did you think the children would let you go so easily?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I'll think of something.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I've heard you're completely incapable of saying 'no' to the children.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Who could ever imagine that the first Nurturer the Matriarch nurtured, one whose diligence and piety are beyond question, was once a criminal who violated the Law?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I'm only attending the family gathering of a friend I've not seen in a long time, Your Eminence.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I told you, no need to be nervous. I'm not worried about you burning Laterano while blowing a balloon or baking a cake.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I'm just curious. Why is there such a stark difference between how the Matriarch sees you, and your profile in the Curia's records?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The Matriarch has never overlooked or denied my sins, Your Eminence. She simply places more importance on my understanding with her.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It was before she became Matriarch. Our paths crossed by sheer chance, when I was taking refuge from a Catastrophe in an abandoned nomadic abbey.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The Matriarch may be blind, but her sense of hearing is impeccable. She caught a faint cry coming from the basement, in the midst of the deafening roar of Originium dashing against the distant mountains.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: A mother, lying in a pool of blood in the shadows on death's door. She attempted to intimidate the Matriarch and protect her own child, but all she managed was an expression of great pain.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: The mother you and the Matriarch first brought to the Holy City? Her injuries were such that even the most determined physician would have given up hope.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: What made you think she would live?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I didn't... I didn't even think she would last the night. But the Matriarch had faith in a miracle, as though it was an inevitability.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The Matriarch wanted me to believe too, believe that the poor mother would find salvation, thanks to us.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: And she did... at first, without medical training, all I could do was empathize and be by her side, caring for her in what ways I could.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: You lingered in a stranded abbey for three months, for the sake of a miracle?

spans.text: You lingered in a stranded abbey for three months, for the sake of a

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: ...Laterano needs a miracle.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Then you're much more rational than I thought, both of you. Perhaps I should see you in a different light.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Certainly, if it convinces the Curia to offer greater support for the Shrine of Nurtury.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: So rational it's almost boring.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Hurry along now, Nurturer Andoain. At the very least, I hope to see the Nativity through without a hitch.
